title: macOS Metal command-encoder crash on viewer resize
description:
Similar to IX-10 (which was about SIGSEGV in AppleMetalOpenGLRenderer on aggressive resize), but a different Metal assertion surface:

  -[AGXG15XFamilyCommandBuffer renderCommandEncoderWithDescriptor:]:963:
    failed assertion 'A command encoder is already encoding to this command buffer'

Exit 134 (SIGABRT). Repros by launching the mesh-viewer profile and resizing the window. The crash happens deep inside Apple's LWJGL OpenGL-on-Metal shim; the mesh renders fine before resize (verified on 22107-vert skull DSL).

Not caused by VIEW-5 tagged-rendering changes — the render() code path taken before any patch overlay is toggled is functionally identical to the pre-VIEW-5 code (one meshShader.use() + one glDrawElements for the untagged case). Resize crash is independent of the new conditional logic.

Possible remediation options:
1. Disable window resize entirely (set glfwWindowHint to fixed size).
2. Queue an explicit glFinish() / context flush on the resize callback before any rendering resumes.
3. Recreate the GL context on resize (heavy but clean).
4. Document as Apple limitation and pin initial window size via -Dixdar.window.width/height.

Workaround today: don't resize the mesh viewer window while it's running. Close and relaunch if you need different dimensions.

Related: IX-10 (prior SIGSEGV flavor, documented as Apple limitation).
definition-of-done: Either: (a) resize works cleanly on macOS arm64, or (b) documented limitation with a CLAUDE.md note + initial-size flags.
testing-plan: (1) Launch via Desktop/Ixdar Mesh Viewer.command. (2) Try resizing: slow drag, then fast drag, then diagonal-corner drag. (3) Verify no Metal assertion.
